Intro.description: I love bringing digital experiences to life through code & design – currently deepening my expertise in the Master’s program for Interactive Technologies.

About.title: About Me
About.description: During my Bachelor's degree in Media Informatics at TH Nürnberg, I gained a strong foundation in computer science and digital media. After graduating, I wanted to further specialize in web development, which led me to pursue a Master's degree in Interactive Technologies with a focus on Mobile at FH St. Pölten. My main focus is on understanding user experience (UX) and translating it into user-centered designs. I am currently looking for a part-time position to further develop my technical skills and deepen my interest in UI design.
About.hobbies: In my free time, I am committed to sustainability and enjoy vegan cooking and baking. I love being in nature — whether hiking in the mountains, road cycling, or bikepacking to discover new places and countries. Last year, for example, I cycled from Roth to Budapest and explored Denmark and Sweden.

timeParabox.description: Interactive puzzle game with escape-box elements and a time travel theme, controlled by a native app.

project.title: The Project
text: Time Parabox is an interactive escape-box game that takes players on an exciting time-travel adventure to resolve paradoxes in history. The journey spans five historical eras – Antiquity, the Middle Ages, the Renaissance, the Industrial Revolution, and World War II.

concept.title: The Concept
text: Each era is represented by a physical puzzle box featuring elements such as NFC tags, magnetic locks, 3D-printed models, a rotary knob, servo motor, and LED ring.

A companion app guides players through the puzzles, connecting the physical components with digital interactions. Each puzzle is thematically aligned with its respective era. The ultimate goal is to solve the puzzles, stabilize the timeline, and save the future.

story.title: The Storyline
text: In a future where time has fallen apart, your future self sends you a mysterious box through a portal. Inside, clues reveal a distorted past—history’s greatest moments have been altered. The steam engine was never invented, Odysseus never returned home. Only you can fix the chaos.

Guided by messages from your future self, you travel through different eras, solving puzzles and collecting artifacts to restore the correct timeline. But in the end, the greatest revelation awaits: the mysterious person who set you on this journey... is you.

implementation.title: Implementation
text: The development process was structured using agile methodologies. Two-week sprints were organized in Jira, and progress was regularly reviewed in weekly meetings.

The app was developed using React Native, with React Redux for state management and Expo for simple setup and efficient testing. Communication between the puzzle box and the companion app was facilitated by an ESP microcontroller, which transmitted data via Bluetooth (BLE) between the app and the electronic components of the boxes.

myTasks.title: My Tasks
text: My main responsibility was developing the app using React Native. In addition to general app development, I contributed to the implementation of specific puzzle mechanics.

For Antiquity, I developed the integration of a digital compass that guided players to help Odysseus find the right path. In the Renaissance era, I implemented an accelerometer mechanic that enabled players to navigate obstacles using Leonardo da Vinci’s flying machine. For the World War II section, I co-designed a puzzle requiring players to decipher Morse codes to obtain the final artifact.

presentation.title: The Presentation
text: Together with a fellow student, I organized the presentation of Time Parabox at the project exhibition of FH St. Pölten. We designed the exhibition booth, created postcards, stickers, flyers, and posters, and developed the logo along with a cohesive corporate design.

Additionally, we created a social media concept for LinkedIn and Instagram to enhance the project’s visibility. Our goal was to develop a consistent and engaging presentation that sparks curiosity and encourages visitors to experience the game firsthand.

bevry.description: A web app for cocktail enthusiasts to discover, share, rate, and manage drinks.

project.title: The Project
text: Bevry is a web app created during my master's studies together with four fellow students. The application is aimed at cocktail enthusiasts who enjoy trying new drink creations and sharing their own recipes.
Initially, we focused on the basic functions: viewing, posting, liking, and rating cocktail recipes.

features.title: Features
text: In the second semester of the master's program, we gave the app a new design and added numerous new features to further improve the user experience.

With the new bar inventory feature, users can always keep track of their existing ingredients. Additionally, recommendations based on the ingredients available in the bar stock were integrated. The shopping list simplifies shopping by allowing missing ingredients to be added directly from the recipe. Users can now also create their own ingredients and add substitute ingredients to make recipes even more personalized.
For entertainment at parties, our two mini-games come into play. One is the turn-based multiplayer game 'Spin the Wheel', and the other is the single-player game 'Mix it Up'.

branding.title: Branding
text: In the course 'Brand Identity & Corporate Design', the corporate identity of Bevry was developed. We worked with Adobe InDesign, Adobe Photoshop, and Figma.
I created the logo, various business stationery, stickers, website designs, and mockups.
Take a look at the brand book!

team.title: Agile Teamwork
text: The team consists of five master's students from FH St. Pölten: Laura, Sara, Sophia, Vani, and me.

We worked with Scrum to stay organized. Sprint Planning and Sprint Review took place every two weeks during our weekly meetings. We used Jira to create tickets and track their status on the Kanban board.

collaboration.title: Interdisciplinary Collaboration
text: We also collaborated with students from other master's programs, including 'Photography' for cocktail, marketing, and portfolio photos, 'Graphic Design' for app design and icons, 'Sound Design' for soundtracks and sound effects for the mini-games, and 'Animation' for a loading animation as well as animations within the mini-games.

myTasks.title: My Tasks
text: My main responsibility was in backend development with NestJS. Endpoint documentation was done using OpenAPI in Swagger. In the backend, I was responsible for the implementation of recipes, ingredients, substitute ingredients, as well as the shopping list and bar inventory. I also handled user data management and the implementation of email verification.
Additionally, I was involved in frontend development with Vue.js. I assisted in implementing the new screen designs and integrated both the self-designed icons and the loading animation.

erika.description: An app as a digital companion for climate-friendly actions and regional activities.

project.title: The Project
text: In the second semester of my master's program, I had the opportunity to work on a research project affiliated with the program's research institute. I chose the ERIKA project. The goal of the project is to develop the ERIKA app, which serves as a digital companion for climate-conscious actions in everyday life.

app.title: The App
text: The app aims to promote climate-friendly behavior and highlight regional activities in the Waidhofen a/d Ybbs area. The focus is not only on sustainable content but also on sustainable aspects in the development and design of the app, ensuring a holistic implementation of the concept of sustainability.

implementation.title: The Implementation
text: During my work on the ERIKA research project, I conducted extensive research on the factors crucial for developing a sustainable website.

Additionally, I participated in researching and formulating research questions related to climate-friendly actions in daily life, the impacts of various measures, the role of digitalization, and the application of gamification to support sustainable behavior.
I analyzed and processed survey results and created a clickable prototype of the app.

sustainability.title: Sustainable Web & App Design
text: Sustainability is crucial in many aspects of life, yet we rarely consider how much the internet impacts our planet. Its CO₂ emissions are equivalent to those of aviation, accounting for about 2% of global emissions.
While researching sustainable web, app, and email design, I discovered various key factors, including hosting, efficient code, optimized images, thoughtful design, and the choice of colors and fonts.

Sustainable web design is not only environmentally beneficial but also enhances user experience, search engine rankings, and accessibility. Websites that consume fewer resources load faster, improving performance, user satisfaction, and overall reach.

prototyping.title: Prototyping
text: I created a Figma prototype for a user story of the ERIKA service. This interactive mockup demonstrates how the service informs users about sustainable initiatives.

The prototype includes a form for submitting initiatives, which appear in the calendar and map view after review. This allows users not only to participate in events but also to contribute their own ideas, increasing their ecological handprint.

The calendar and map views display upcoming initiatives and events. Each event has a detailed page with descriptions, dates, and location info. With GPS enabled, users receive notifications when near an event.

ecocalypse.description: Creation of an immersive video game scene in Unity focusing on worldbuilding and visual storytelling.

project.title: The Project
text: In my second master's semester, I participated in a one-week Summer School workshop. I chose Environmental Storytelling, which focused on worldbuilding as well as environmental and visual storytelling.

The project involved creating a static or interactive immersive video game scene using Unity and pre-made assets. The scene needed to be realistic, visually engaging, and functional for a game environment, with a strong emphasis on applying the principles of environmental storytelling.

In small teams, we developed Ecocalypse, a game set in 2035 after a climate catastrophe. A year earlier, the entire rainforest had burned down, triggering climate collapse and the breakdown of the global order.

implementation.title: The Implementation
text: For the implementation of the project, I took on several tasks, including worldbuilding, storytelling, and placing objects in the room, such as the newspaper articles. Additionally, I was responsible for selecting the necessary low-poly assets for Unity.

When creating the storyline, we paid special attention to integrating behavioral traces, identity claims, and mood modifiers. These elements had to be cohesive to create an immersive experience. Any inconsistencies in the room, lighting, or sound could break the players’ immersion and disrupt the experience.

scene.title: The Scene
text: The scene is set in a room of an elegant house that was once Joseph’s office. After the unexpected collapse of infrastructure, he barricaded himself there, waiting for the right time to escape to the countryside to reunite with his family.

The player discovers traces of his daily life and preparations for escape, including personal belongings, notes, and supplies. The room is ransacked and bears the marks of a violent raid in which Joseph was killed for his resources. Now, the intruders are using his supplies, while the room paints a vivid picture of Joseph’s desperate struggle for survival and his tragic demise.

objects.title: The Objects
text: Carefully placed objects narrate the game's story and provide background context. Newspaper articles on the walls report on the crisis. A family portrait hints at a rural safe haven. A city map highlights Joseph’s planned escape route.

A wall calendar marks January 2035, showing Joseph’s attempts to keep track of time. His detailed daily routine reflects his struggle against isolation. An unfinished letter to Julia reveals his thoughts and emotions. An ad for H2-NO underscores extreme water scarcity and the world's dire conditions.
These elements create an immersive scene that effectively applies the principles of environmental storytelling.

veganAdvent.description: A digital advent calendar with valuable tips and information for a vegan lifestyle.

project.title: The Project
text: The idea behind this advent calendar was to present new information or helpful tips about veganism each day in December. I intentionally chose not to include a feature that checks the current day, ensuring that the website's content is always accessible as part of the 'Print to Mobile' project for my master's program at FH St. Pölten. My goal was not only to share recipes but also to raise awareness of the benefits of a vegan lifestyle.

poster.title: The Poster
text: Additionally, there is a poster with 24 numbered QR codes. Each day in December, users can scan the QR code for the respective day to access the corresponding advent door.

implementation.title: The Implementation
text: I developed the web application using React and Tailwind CSS. The interactive bar chart in door 2 was created with ApexCharts.
On the website, users can switch between Light Mode, Dark Mode, and the system’s default display mode. The colors of the SVG on the homepage also adapt to the selected mode.
More information about the project and the commented source code for my implemented components can be found on GitHub.

trilum.description: Analysis and redesign of the user interface for the wireless Pick-by-Light system TRILUM to enhance usability.

project.title: The Project
text: As part of my bachelor's thesis, I analyzed and redesigned the graphical user interface of the Pick-by-Light system TRILUM. The system, developed by the Fraunhofer Society at the Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Circuits (IIS), served as the foundation for my work.

In collaboration with Fraunhofer IIS, where I was hired as a student assistant in the Supply Chain Services group in Nuremberg following my mandatory internship, I had the opportunity to write my bachelor's thesis. My goal was to improve the usability of the web application.
Access to my bachelor's thesis is password-protected — just reach out to me for the login details

init.title: Starting Point
text: TRILUM is a wireless Pick-by-Light system for warehouse picking and assembly processes. The system guides employees who need to retrieve materials from shelves to the correct compartment using light signals.
However, the focus of my work was on the desktop application developed using the Angular framework. This application is used to coordinate orders, manage inventory, and oversee employees.

implementation.title: Implementation
text: To emphasize user-centricity, the user-centered design process according to ISO standard 9241/210 was applied.
First, the application was analyzed. During this phase, other Pick-by-Light systems were reviewed, and user requirements were documented.

To design and conduct usability tests, appropriate usability evaluation methods were selected. Users were surveyed using a questionnaire, and the think-aloud method was employed to observe user behavior.

Based on the test evaluations, usability issues were identified, and design solutions were developed to improve the user experience. The optimization proposals were then prioritized and implemented in the existing system, followed by a second round of usability testing.

result.title: The Result
text: The results of the follow-up tests show that the system's usability was significantly improved, allowing for more intuitive interaction. Participants not only found the tasks easier to complete but also rated the interaction principles much higher.

nakt.description: WordPress website without pre-built themes or plugins. The focus was on PHP programming.

project.title: The Project
text: NAKT? Interested? NAKT is the name of a WordPress website that I developed together with three classmates as part of a study project in the sixth semester. The name is derived from the first letters of our first names.

What makes this website special is that no pre-built themes, plugins, shortcodes, etc., were used, as these had to be programmed independently. The focus was on PHP development, although HTML, JavaScript, and CSS were also utilized. I also made sure that the content could be displayed in both German and English by implementing localization.

implementation.title: The Implementation
text: For the project, I developed a 'Recipes' plugin, allowing the user to create their own recipes. I also programmed a widget with various configuration options, which displays posts randomly. The user can also submit sustainability tips, for which I developed a JSON export.
Further information about the project and the commented source code of my implemented components can be found on GitHub.
